hypotheses.claim: A provenance-bound Visual State Transition Graph represented as canonical UnifiedDB transition records plus derived ClayGraph topology can reduce repeated full Qwen GUI reasoning by retrieving previously verified state-action-outcome transitions from current visual/task evidence.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: This could turn Frank experience into executable perceptual structure while preserving the one-module and single-semantic-architecture constraints.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: GUI states are too partially observable and visually aliased for transition reuse; graph retrieval will increase stale/incorrect action proposals and hidden-operation blindness.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched held-out GUI episodes show no net task/latency/token benefit, or wrong-action/stale-state rates exceed QWEN_ONLY/PAR baselines after alias and mismatch gates.
hypotheses.cheapest_discriminating_test: Offline replay over frozen pre-action/action/post-action episodes comparing QWEN_ONLY, PAR_EAP, VSTG_VISUAL_ONLY and VSTG_TASK_BOUND without permitting real effects.
hypotheses.expected_signature_if_true: Fewer full decoder calls/tokens and equal-or-better task-state/action correctness; transition retrieval precision rises with verified experience dose; wrong-seed controls collapse benefit.
hypotheses.expected_signature_if_false: High visual alias conflict, stale transition reuse, little decoder-call reduction, or benefit disappears when direct-memory baseline is matched.

hypotheses.claim: When one high-confidence visual fingerprint maps to multiple incompatible task states, next actions or verified outcomes, an explicit VISUAL_ALIAS_CONFLICT gate can make transition memory safer than naive nearest-state reuse by forcing task-state binding, active sensing or full semantic escalation.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: Alias conflicts are too frequent or too difficult to detect from available context, so the gate degenerates into near-constant escalation and eliminates the efficiency benefit.
hypotheses.falsifier: Conflict gate recall is low on hidden-state fixtures or escalation rate becomes high enough that VSTG no longer beats QWEN_ONLY/PAR on total pathway cost.
hypotheses.cheapest_discriminating_test: Construct paired screenshots with same/near-same visual state but different task/subgoal/history/outcome semantics and measure conflict detection and safe abstention.

hypotheses.claim: Persistent task/progress state should remain semantically separate from transient PerceptualField state, and only verified action/outcome receipts may advance task state; visual similarity alone must never imply task progress.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: Existing Frank self/world/goal state already provides sufficient separation, making a dedicated transition test invariant useful but not an architecture delta.
hypotheses.falsifier: Current H1/H2 state model already enforces equivalent semantics and differential tests show no additional failures captured by the explicit invariant.
hypotheses.cheapest_discriminating_test: Replay stale/repeated screenshots after failed/no-op actions and assert task-state non-advancement until verified outcome.

hypotheses.claim: Where available, binding Qwen/MVC visual fingerprints to deterministic app/window/URL/accessibility/source metadata will reduce state aliasing versus pixels/features alone without creating a second semantic authority channel.
hypotheses.strongest_counterhypothesis: Nonvisual metadata is brittle, unavailable across many surfaces, privacy-sensitive or overfits specific applications; visual-only plus task-state context may be Pareto-superior.
hypotheses.falsifier: Hybrid metadata fails to reduce alias errors or adds enough coupling/latency/failure modes to lose under equal-budget cross-application testing.
hypotheses.cheapest_discriminating_test: Compare VISUAL_ONLY versus HYBRID_FINGERPRINT on visually identical/near-identical but semantically distinct UI states, with metadata removed/shuffled as controls.
